title: Metabolic Profiling to Determine Bactericidal or Bacteriostatic Effects of New Natural Products using Isothermal Microcalorimetry
protocol: Streak out the strain under investigation on a CASO agar plate and incubate overnight in a static incubator at 30 °C.
Inoculate a single colony into MHB and incubate on a shaking incubator at 180 rpm at 30 °C to prepare an overnight culture.
Prepare concentration ranges of selected drug or compound using 1.5 mL tubes.
Measure the optical density of the overnight culture using a spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 600 nm.
Dilute the culture to obtain 5 x 10^5 CFU/mL in fresh MHB medium.
Add 150 μL of cells to test tubes prepared earlier, ensuring correct final concentrations of tested drug or compound and cell concentration.
Mix the compound with the cells by vortexing.
Transfer 120 μL from the mixture to the plastic inserts using reverse pipetting.
Place titanium vials into holders with tweezers.
Gently transfer inserts into the titanium vials in the holder plate.
Loosely place titanium lids on all titanium vials.
Transfer the holder with titanium cups onto the sample station and place it in the designated area.
Use the torque wrench set to 40 cNm force to tighten all the lids.
In calView software, start a new experiment.
Retract the sample insertion arm from the instrument.
Place the cup holder on the “bridge”, column 8 facing the sample insertion opening.
Gently push the cup holder into the instrument at the designated “Position 1”.
Wait 10 minutes for the system to stabilize.
Label the experimental wells.
Push the sample insertion arm until the cup holder is at the designated “Position 2”.
Wait 20 minutes for the system to stabilize.
Push the sample insertion arm into “Position 3”.
Retract the sample insertion arm until it is at the “Running position”.
Highlight all the wells in the software and select Reaction Start.
Run the experiment until the heat emission reads are stably back at zero.
If all wells behave similarly, proceed to remove the cup holder.
In the software, select Stop.
Select Yes when prompted if you are sure.
Save the experiment on a drive or desktop for data analysis.
Insert the sample insertion arm completely into the instrument and engage the magnets to retrieve the cup holder.
Loosen the lids.
Remove the inserts.
Place vials and lids into glass holders.
Place the vials and lids in an oven at 180 °C for 4 hours.
Place the vials and lids into a desiccator to ensure lids and vials are dry.
Open the software.
Select Open experiment in the left upper corner.
In the popup window, select the experiment of interest and press Open.
The application will open the experiment in default wells view.
Press Select all or use Ctrl+A.
Press Define Baseline to normalize data at each position.
In the popup window, select a time period of >30 min located in the lag phase with low heat flow (between zero and ten µW).
After selection, the chosen baseline will appear in green in the thermogram.
Close the Define Baseline Section window.
Press Save or use Ctrl+S to save the data.
Close the software.
Open web-based Symcel Calorimetry analysis application.
To upload the file, press Browse.
Select the experiment and press Open.
The metabolic parameters will be calculated automatically for 32 samples in the web application.
Click Growth Function to fit heat Flow data to Gompertz and/or Richard’s growth models.
Growth models fit will be displayed in the “Cumulative” section and compared to raw data in the “Flow” section.
